correctness.rationale: The odd-part definition makes every symbol with argument m not divisible by 16 depend only on m modulo 32; any length≤15 window contains at most one multiple of 16. Therefore 32 residue classes times one exceptional bit give an exhaustive 64-state finite representation. Each of the two exceptional values has conditional density 1/2 by odd-part valuation residues, giving state weight 1/64. Independently computed all 64×15 windows and their reverse tests: exactly 28 palindromic words at lengths 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,9,11,13, with multiplicities respectively 32,16,4,8,4,2,2,2,1,1 per word and none at 8,10,12,14,15. Any longer even/odd palindrome contains centered length14/15, so none occur. This is an exact exhaustive finite-state certificate linked by a proof to infinite factors, not a finite-prefix extrapolation.
residual_risks: Only the regular binary folding convention or its global complement; no assertion for arbitrary instructions. Longest-palindrome cutoff was known previously.

originality.rationale: The 2001/2003 Allouche–Baake–Cassaigne–Damanik primary article establishes the absence of paperfolding palindromes of length≥14 (Theorem 4), a bound explicitly credited here. Its Section 4.1 does not give individual finite palindrome occurrence densities or exact residue-state positions. Resultary searches find related generalized-paperfolding run frequencies and exact palindrome statistics for other automatic words, but no independent prior 28-word individual table of this specified regular paperfolding word. The exact 64-state weighted occurrence classification is thus a distinct best-of-knowledge invariant.
residual_risks: An unindexed older paper may tabulate all individual paperfolding palindrome occurrence densities; Resultary semantic search is not proof of historical absence.

value.rationale: Exact natural densities of all 28 named palindromes and a position-level congruence rule are a natural finer invariant than palindrome complexity. Equal frequencies within each length reveal specific arithmetic symmetry; this complete classification of a standard automatic sequence is a potentially reusable exact dataset, not merely an arbitrary small-slice statistic.
residual_risks: Known length≥14 exclusion is only an input; finite residue certificate is justified by the all-starts reduction.

final_claim: The standard binary regular paperfolding word has exactly 28 nonempty ordinary palindrome factors, no palindrome of length≥14, and equal exact starting-position densities for each word at a fixed length; a 64-state residue/exception-bit classification computes all words and occurrences.
limitations: One particular regular folding-instruction sequence and global complement, not every generalized paperfolding word.
Exact finite-state extraction proves unlimited starting positions and weights; finite direct prefix samples are supplementary.
The absence of length≥14 palindromes is known from Allouche et al., not newly claimed.
